doc: Log-log slope of the radially averaged power spectrum: (patch - mean) * Hann (np.hanning(n) outer itself, symmetric, 0.5 - 0.5 cos(2 pi i / (n - 1))), np.fft.fft2 (unnormalized, complex128), fftshift, |F|^2, radius r = int(hypot(x, y)) with x, y counted from n // 2 (truncation), radial[r] = mean of the power at integer radius r (np.bincount), wavelength of bin k = n * patch_px_km() / k km; bins with lo <= wavelength <= hi (inclusive) and radial > 0 enter np.polyfit(log k, log radial, 1), whose slope is returned; fewer than 4 bins give NaN. n = patch.shape[0] (square patches only). The DEFAULT band (the call omits lo_km and hi_km; Python defaults 40 and 400 km, repeated in params). n = 137: the bin k = 3 has wavelength 400.79 km, just ABOVE 400 (excluded), and k = 30 has 40.08 km, just ABOVE 40 (included): a default hi_km of 404 or a default lo_km of 40.4 gives another slope. Smoothed noise (sigma 1.5), odd prime size (Bluestein FFT in numpy). The whole chain is float64 (the Hann window is float64 even for a float32 patch): an independent float64 reimplementation agrees to 9e-16 with np.fft and to 1.4e-13 with an explicit DFT-matrix product (a different operation order; measured on Earth patches, noise and smooth fields), a float64 one-ulp nudge of the texels moves the slope by <= 1.7e-15; tolerance 1e-9.
